To export from code, ask for the file’s contents or write it:

code: let data = await table.exportedData(as: .xlsx, options: GHExportOptions(rows: .selected))

inlineContent.text: An export has the visible columns in display order (but those in
, e.g. a column of row numbers) and the
rows shown (filtered, sorted, without group headers), or the selected ones,
and the summary row. CSV has the displayed texts, in UTF-8 with a byte order mark so
Excel reads any language. The workbook keeps numbers, dates and check marks
as values, in number formats like the columns’ (currency, percent, fraction
digits), with a bold header row that stays in view and the columns’ widths.
Values are read in slices, keeping the app responsive (
and written into the file as they come, formatted (and for a workbook,
compressed) on all cores: an export holds a chunk of rows, not the file, and
the file appears when it is done. A million rows of 20 columns take about
3.5 s as a workbook or as CSV, with about 50–110 MB more memory meanwhile.
builds the file in memory: for large tables write it with

selected rows are exported.
